clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old man presented with a 4-year progressive history of dermatophytosis caused by T. interdigitale, initially appearing near the left eyebrow and gradually spreading to the face, trunk, and limbs. Clinical examination revealed extensive erythematous plaques with clear borders and scales, scattered red papules with ulceration, scabs, and onychomycosis on the left hand nails. Concurrent fungal keratitis developed 2 years after cutaneous disease onset, presenting with conjunctival infection, secretion, and corneal ulceration. Vision loss in the left eye occurred approximately 1 year before admission. Mycological investigation confirmed T. interdigitale through KOH mount (hyaline septate hyphae), fungal culture (white downy colonies with branched septate hyphae and spherical-to-pyriform microconidia), and PCR-ITS sequencing (99% identity with T. interdigitale reference strain CBS 428.63T) from skin, nail, and corneal specimens. The patient was treated with luliconazole cream (two applications daily) and itraconazole (100 mg BID orally) for 1 month, with significant improvement observed after 14 days. Left eye enucleation was subsequently performed due to irreversible vision loss. No recurrence was documented during 3-month follow-up.
